0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 June 1963, after the draft finalized by the Man-Made Fibre and Fabric Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Packing plays a very important part in the safe transport of goods Proper packaging with appropriate and their storage and marketing. quality of packing materials protects the goods from the hazards of transit, provides for easier handling and preserves the contents from This code gives details of seaworthy infestation and other deterioration. packaging of man-made fibre fabrics which would ensure adequate protection to the contents of the bale or case. 0.3 The details of packaging balrs or cases given in this code do not In case goods apply to man-made fibre fabrics intended for surf ports. are to be unloaded at surf ports, necessary provision for special packing of bales or cases may be made in the contract. 0.4 Considerable assistance has been derived from the followinr; fications and from the data supplied by the Silk and Art Silk Research Association, Bombay, in the preparation of this code: specihiills'

INDIA. MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY. 1. SCOPE
1.1 This code prescribes the method fabrics intended for transport by sea. 3 of packaging man-made fibre

IS : 2194 - 1963 2. PACKING PROCEDURE

2.1 Grey Cloth in Bales 2.1.1 Plait and fold each piece of cloth. Take a sufficient number of such pieces and arrange them on the table of the baling press over layers of packing materials (see 2.1.2) to form a bale of rectangular or square shape. Place on the top of the bale similar layers of packing materials so as to cover the contents.
2.1.2 \Yrap Table I: the bale in layers of packing materials listed in

a) using materials which are sound, clean and in dry condition, and which, in quality, conform to the applicable requirements of Appendix A; b) following the sequence of the listing, so that when a bale is finally made up, the material listed first forms the inner layer and the material listed last forms the outer layer; and c) laying pieces of the materials, so that they cover the bale with adequate overlaps while it is under pressure in the baling press.

2.3 Finished Cloth in Cases 2.3.1 Plait and fold each piece or wrap it on wooden rollers or cardboard tubes of suitable size and thickness. Wrap each piece in materials, such as strong paper, cellophane or polythene film, etc, which will not stain the fabric. Place a sufficient number of such tubes or pieces in a packing case which:
a) complies with the applicable requirements of Appendix A; b) is lined with layers of packing materials given in Table II so that when the case is fully lined up, the hessian-lined krnft paper or the waterproof paper or the polythene film forms the outer layer and the kraft paper or the sulphite paper forms the inner layer; and c) together with the cloth safely transported.
